question: A 47-year-old man comes to the physician because of abdominal pain and foul-smelling, watery diarrhea for several days. He has not had nausea, vomiting, or blood in the stool. He has a history of alcohol use disorder and recently completed a 7-day course of clindamycin for pneumonia. He has not traveled out of the United States. Which of the following toxins is most likely to be involved in the pathogenesis of this patient's symptoms?
analysis: The patient's symptoms of abdominal pain and foul-smelling, watery diarrhea following a course of clindamycin are highly suggestive of Clostridioides difficile infection. Clindamycin is a well-known antibiotic that can disrupt normal gut flora, leading to overgrowth of C. difficile. The toxins produced by C. difficile, particularly the cytotoxins, are responsible for the symptoms. This aligns with the clinical presentation and history provided.
